text: Bounded knapsack (多重背包): item i may be taken up to mi times. Treating each copy as its own 0/1 item costs O(W Σ m). Binary splitting (二进制拆分): split m into 1, 2, 4, …, 2k, rest. Every count from 0 to m is a sum of some of these pieces, so 0/1 knapsack over the pieces is equivalent: O(W Σ log m).

Even faster, O(W·n): for each item, group capacities by remainder mod w; inside a group the transition is "best over the last m values" of a shifted sequence, a monotone queue (进阶篇第18章). Binary splitting is usually enough and much shorter.
Treasures (P1776): value, weight, count per item. Checked against the copy-by-copy DP in Python.

Why it works: with pieces 1, 2, 4 and rest 3 (for m = 10) every number 0 … 10 is reachable, and no combination exceeds 10. Mixed problems (P1833 樱花): treat count 1 as 0/1, "unlimited" as complete knapsack, others by splitting.

wqs binary search (WQS 二分 , "Aliens trick"): to find the best answer using exactly k of something, when best(k) is convex in k. Add a penalty λ to each use and solve without the constraint, which is easy: the number of uses in the optimum moves monotonically with λ. Binary search λ until the optimum uses k, then remove the penalty: answer = result − λ·k.

Tree I (P2619): minimum spanning tree with exactly need white edges. Add λ to every white edge's cost and run Kruskal (whites first on ties). Larger λ means fewer whites, so binary search λ and take the cost back off at the end. The exact rule for ties is what makes the answer correct.

The second test is a random graph checked against Python trying every spanning tree. Pick the largest λ that still gives ≥ need whites (with whites preferred on ties): at that λ an optimal tree with exactly need whites has the same cost, so cost − λ·need is right even if this run used more.

wqs only works when best(k) is convex (each extra unit helps less, or hurts more). Check it on small cases by brute force before trusting it. Penalties must be integers here because costs are integers; the search range must cover every possible slope.

Knuth's optimisation (四边形不等式优化): in an interval DP f[l][r] = mink f[l][k] + f[k+1][r] + w(l, r), let opt[l][r] be the best split. When w satisfies the quadrangle inequality and is monotone on nested intervals (true for "sum of the segment"), opt[l][r−1] ≤ opt[l][r] ≤ opt[l+1][r]. Searching only that range makes the total O(n²) instead of O(n³).
The ranges telescope: for a fixed length, Σ (opt[l+1][r] − opt[l][r−1] + 1) is O(n), so each length costs O(n). Merging stones in a line (进阶篇第15章) drops from O(n³) to O(n²) with three changed lines.
Checked against the plain O(n³) interval DP in Python. opt[i][i] = i starts the chain; the cap min(r − 1, …) keeps k a valid split.
The maximum version of stone merging does not satisfy the condition: there the best split is always at one end instead. Prove or test the monotonicity of opt by brute force before using it.

Related tools: divide and conquer optimisation when opt is monotone in a layered DP f[i][j] = mink f[i−1][k] + cost(k, j) (O(kn log n)); SMAWK / 1D1D with a deque of candidates for f[i] = minj f[j] + w(j, i) with a convex w (诗人小 G).
